chapter: Neighborhood halls and the Ida Cox tour
title: Nervous in Paul Barbarin's big band
summary: He recalls that when Paul Barbarin formed a big band he was too nervous to cut the trombone parts, but remains loyal to him.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Well there's something I want to tell you too Bill. You remember when, I guess you heard about it, well that's before I went out on the road, when Paul Barberan had a cab in town. Well that was the time they had big bands, you know. Yeah. And he made up a big band. And I'll never forget this old, I think it was Will Hudson, the ramming on some kind of serenade. Oh, Moonlight or something? No, no, it wasn't.
No, no, I was just, they don't know it. Yeah.

Well then I, with all the fellas he had in there, well I couldn't cut it, they needed a trombone fellas, I couldn't cut it. I had gotten nervous, you know. Yeah. And that's when he had the big band. But just go with sure, now I'm with him, you know. Yeah. No matter what happened, I'm with him.
Sure, I know you can cut the stuff now from what I've heard of.
I'll never forget that though. I, at that particular time, I guess I just was nervous, you know.
